note: Machine-readable copy of HYPOTHESES.md. The markdown is the published statement; this file is what the code reads. tests/test_preregistration.py fails if they disagree.

window.anchor: newest partition shared by every table we query

bot_filter.balance_source: account_changes (amended by A2); yoctoNEAR, divided by 1e24

verdict_rule.method: ordinary least squares slope on the monthly series
verdict_rule.supported: 95% CI entirely in the predicted direction, and every extra bar met
verdict_rule.rejected: 95% CI entirely in the opposite direction

robustness_labels.robust: every grid cell agrees with the prediction
robustness_labels.depends: some cells agree, others are flat or disagree
robustness_labels.reversed: no cell agrees and at least one points the other way

hypotheses.name: Real usage
hypotheses.metric: count of economic accounts per 30-day window, monthly, at default thresholds
hypotheses.rejected_if: 95% CI of the slope lies entirely below zero at default thresholds

hypotheses.name: Concentration
hypotheses.metric: top-10 receiver share of economic transactions, and HHI on the 0-1 scale, monthly
hypotheses.rejected_if: 95% CI of either slope lies entirely above zero

hypotheses.name: Retention
hypotheses.metric: share of each monthly cohort still economic at exactly +3 months, point-in-time
hypotheses.rejected_if: 95% CI of the slope across cohort months lies entirely below zero
hypotheses.left_censoring: the first cohort of the window is excluded from the headline trend (amendment A3)

hypotheses.name: Cross-chain shift
hypotheses.metric: cross-chain settlement share, monthly; count form is the headline, value form secondary
hypotheses.rejected_if: 95% CI of the slope lies entirely below zero
hypotheses.lower_bound: Intents Explorer API covers 1Click swaps only; both legs are lower bounds on their own side

forms.count_headline: intents_swaps / (intents_swaps + native_economic_transfers), pricing-free; the native leg is filtered by the same economic-account definition as H1
forms.value_secondary: intents_usd / (intents_usd + native_usd); intents_usd comes from the API's amountInUsd, native_usd covers only contracts priceable by an a priori rule, with coverage reported as a percentage

hypotheses.disagreement_rule: if the count and value forms disagree in direction, report both and treat H4 as INCONCLUSIVE
hypotheses.why_count_is_headline: ft_events has no decimals column, so the native USD leg needs outside metadata for every contract while the Intents leg needs none; the headline must not rest on the weaker leg
hypotheses.why_economic_filter_in_denominator: a one-day feasibility probe found NEP-141 transfer counts dominated by two reward-token applications, so an unfiltered denominator would track a reward schedule rather than settlement
hypotheses.unique_swappers_caveat: the senders field is sometimes an empty array; the share of swaps with an identifiable sender is reported alongside the count

sampling.reported_as: per-day rate with a confidence interval across the four sampled days

H5a.metric: monthly fees burned vs new issuance, and net issuance = issuance - burned

extra_bars.name: materiality
extra_bars.test: burned fees >= 10% of gross issuance in the window's final month

H5a.rejected_if: the materiality bar fails AND the slope's 95% CI does not lie above zero

H5b.metric: documentary: does any portion of NEAR Intents fees accrue to NEAR token holders
H5b.answered_from: primary sources only, cited in SOURCES.md
H5b.pre_committed_reading: if primary documentation names no mechanism by which Intents fees reach NEAR holders, that counts as evidence AGAINST the claim's second clause and is reported as such

no_new_hypotheses: These five are the only hypotheses tested. Anything found later appears under 'Exploratory (not pre-registered)' and is never counted as evidence for or against the claim.

bull_base_bear.constraint: indicators must be quantities this pipeline already computes

amendments.change: Intents and native legs measured from a stratified sample of 4 days per month (the 5th, 12th, 19th, 26th), 48 days total, reported as per-day rates with a confidence interval
amendments.reason: a census is ~10.5M swaps and over 15 hours at the documented 1-request-per-5-seconds rate limit, which does not fit before the deadline
amendments.bias_risk: rests only on swaps-per-unit-time from the most recent page; no monthly series, ratio or trend was computed first, and the sampled dates are identical in every month
amendments.cost: sampling error, reported as an interval; any day-of-month effect is not averaged out

amendments.change: the b threshold's balance source moves from ft_balances_daily to account_changes, taking each account's balance at its last change inside the window; balances there are yoctoNEAR and are divided by 1e24
amendments.reason: ft_balances_daily matched 3,064 of 816,171 signers (0.38%), so the join tested table membership rather than a balance; raising b from 0 to 0.1 cut the count from 19,855 to 568
amendments.bias_risk: found by checking the threshold grid for internal consistency, not by comparing any trend against a prediction; restores the criterion already specified and leaves the thresholds unchanged
amendments.cost: balance is measured at the account's last change in the window rather than exactly at window end; the query scans ~15 GiB per month instead of ~1 GiB

amendments.change: the first cohort in the window (2025-11) is excluded from the headline trend; both figures are published
amendments.reason: the window has no history before it starts, so every account economic in its first month appears new; that cohort is 3x the next one's size and is both artificially large and artificially loyal
amendments.bias_risk: the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE with or without it, and the exclusion works against a rejection narrative rather than for it
amendments.cost: eight cohort observations instead of nine, and a wider interval
